title: Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals
introLead: 40 questions, 45 minutes. Questions follow the SC-900 study guide order — security, compliance, and identity concepts, Microsoft Entra, security solutions, compliance solutions — then a case study.
introPoints: Two sections: independent questions, then a case study. After you open the case study, you cannot return to the independent questions.
Question types include single choice, multiple choice, drag and drop, build list, active screen, hot area, exhibit, and yes/no.
Nothing is graded while you are in the exam. The score, rationale, and Microsoft Learn link appear at the end.
The score you see is a raw score. The real exam uses a scaled score out of 1,000, and 700 is the passing score. This percentage is not an official result.

domains.label: Describe concepts of security, compliance, and identity
Describe capabilities of Microsoft security solutions
Describe capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions

questions.objective: Describe shared responsibility in the cloud
questions.stem: A company uses a SaaS billing application. Which party is responsible for classifying and protecting the customer records stored in that application?

choices.text: Nobody, because SaaS data is public by design

questions.rationale: In the shared responsibility model, information and data are always the customer's responsibility, at every service layer. The provider runs the application, but never classifies or owns the customer's records.

questions.stem: An organization uses firewalls, patched devices, application controls, and file encryption so that an attacker who passes one layer still faces the next one. Which approach is this?

choices.text: Implicit trust for the internal network

questions.rationale: Defense in depth layers multiple defensive controls — physical, network, device, application, and data — so a breach of one layer is slowed or stopped by the next.

questions.stem: A policy validates user identity, device health, and location on every request, even for requests that arrive from the corporate network. Which zero trust principle does this illustrate?

choices.text: Patch on a fixed yearly schedule

questions.rationale: Verify explicitly means always authenticating and authorizing with all available data — identity, device, and location — instead of trusting a network location. The other zero trust principles are use least privileged access and assume breach.

questions.stem: Which two principles are part of the zero trust model?

choices.text: Trust the corporate network by default
Grant every user the Global Administrator role

questions.rationale: Zero trust stands on verify explicitly, use least privileged access, and assume breach. Trusting a network by default, over-granting roles, and skipping logs all contradict the model.

questions.stem: A regulation requires that health records stay unread to strangers and that nobody can alter them undetected. Which two goals of the CIA triad are named here?
questions.rationale: Keeping records unread to strangers is confidentiality; detecting alteration is integrity. Availability, the third goal, concerns systems being up when needed.

questions.stem: Match each protection need to the concept that satisfies it.

targets.label: Protect a database file that sits on a storage disk.
Protect credentials sent to a website over TLS.
Produce a fixed-length fingerprint that reveals any change in a file.

questions.rationale: Data on a disk is protected with encryption at rest. Data moving across the network needs encryption in transit. Hashing produces a deterministic fingerprint used to detect changes, and it is not encryption.

questions.stem: For a company that operates in the European Union, what kind of requirement is the GDPR?

choices.text: A regulatory policy set by a government
An organizational policy written by the IT team

questions.rationale: Government bodies issue regulatory policies such as the GDPR, and organizations must comply. Organizational and team policies are internal choices that must not conflict with the regulation.

questions.stem: Multifactor authentication adds a second proof when a user signs in. Select the identity process that multifactor authentication strengthens.

regions.label: Identification
regions.detail: The user states who they are, for example with a username.

regions.label: Authentication
regions.detail: The user proves who they are, for example with a password and a phone approval.

regions.label: Authorization
regions.detail: The system decides what the proven user may do.

questions.rationale: Authentication is proving identity. A second factor — something you have or are — strengthens that proof. Identification is only claiming a name and authorization happens after the proof succeeds.

questions.stem: Order the four steps of the access control process from the first to the last.

choices.text: Identification — the user presents a username
Authentication — the user proves the identity
Authorization — the system grants the allowed actions
Accounting — the activity is logged for audit

questions.rationale: Access control runs identification first, then authentication, then authorization, and finally accounting, which records what happened for later audit.

questions.stem: A helpdesk agent must reset user passwords but must not manage licenses or subscriptions. Which principle should guide the role you assign?

choices.text: Separation of duties, so the agent also approves payments
Maximum convenience, so everyone is a Global Administrator

questions.rationale: Least privilege grants only the permissions needed for the task, such as a password-reset role, which limits the damage an account can cause if it is compromised.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft service is the cloud identity and access management service that was formerly named Azure Active Directory?

choices.text: Active Directory Domain Services on a virtual machine

questions.rationale: Microsoft Entra ID is the cloud identity and access management service, the successor in name to Azure Active Directory. AD DS remains a separate on-premises directory service.

questions.stem: A user is signed in. The system now checks the assigned roles before opening the payroll application. Which process is running?
questions.rationale: Authorization decides what an authenticated identity may do, for example through roles. Authentication already proved who the user is; repudiation and spoofing are threat concepts.

questions.stem: Which two options are valid multifactor authentication factor categories?

choices.text: Something you know, such as a password or PIN
Something you have, such as a registered phone or smart card
The city where you were born
The name of your first pet

questions.rationale: The factor categories are something you know, something you have, and something you are. Favorite colors, birthplaces, and pet names are security questions, not MFA factors.

questions.stem: Match each task to the least privileged Microsoft Entra role that can perform it.

targets.label: Reset passwords and create user accounts for the helpdesk.
Create the policies that require multifactor authentication at sign-in.
Review risky sign-ins flagged by Identity Protection and dismiss false positives.

questions.rationale: User Administrator manages accounts and passwords. Conditional Access Administrator owns sign-in policies. Security Administrator handles security data such as risky sign-ins. Billing Administrator is the distractor — it manages subscriptions, not identities.

questions.stem: Employees sign in once in the morning and then open the CRM, the intranet, and email without typing credentials again. Which capability makes this possible?

choices.text: Separate local accounts for each application

questions.rationale: Single sign-on authenticates the user once and reuses that identity across applications, which improves both productivity and security. Password spraying is an attack, not a feature.

questions.stem: Create a Conditional Access policy so that every user must provide a second proof at sign-in. Set both settings.
questions.rationale: The requirement covers every user, so the policy assigns All users, and the grant control requires multifactor authentication. Blocking access would keep everyone out, and granting open access would enforce nothing.

questions.stem: An external accountant must collaborate on documents using her own credentials, without receiving an internal password. Which Microsoft Entra capability fits?

choices.text: B2B collaboration with a guest user
A shared mailbox password for everyone
Creating her as a Global Administrator
Turning off multifactor authentication for partners

questions.rationale: Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration invites external partners as guests who sign in with their own identity while your conditional access policies still apply. Shared passwords and lowered security are the opposite of good practice.

questions.stem: Order the steps of creating a Conditional Access policy from start to finish.

choices.text: Assign the users or groups the policy applies to
Select the cloud applications or actions
Define the access controls, such as requiring MFA
Turn the policy on, after testing in report-only mode

questions.rationale: A Conditional Access policy is built by assigning users, then the target applications, then the grant or session controls, and it goes live only when enabled — ideally after report-only testing.

questions.stem: Review the editions table, then choose the least expensive edition that includes Conditional Access.

exhibits.title: Microsoft Entra ID editions
rows: Free
Single sign-on, basic reports, security defaults
P1
Everything in Free, plus Conditional Access and hybrid identity
P2
Everything in P1, plus Identity Protection with risk-based reports

questions.rationale: The table shows Conditional Access arriving with P1, which is therefore the least expensive edition that includes it. Free stops at security defaults, and P2 adds risk features you do not need here.

questions.stem: Which solution is a cloud-native SIEM that collects telemetry from many sources, correlates it with analytics rules, and lets you respond with playbooks?
questions.rationale: Microsoft Sentinel is the cloud-native security information and event management (SIEM) solution: connectors ingest data, analytics rules detect threats, and playbooks automate the response.

questions.stem: Attacks now cross email, endpoints, and identities in one campaign. Which solution correlates detection and automated response across those domains?
questions.rationale: Microsoft Defender XDR unifies signals from Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, Defender for Identity, and Entra ID into correlated incidents with automated response.

questions.stem: A team wants continuous assessment of the security posture of its Azure and hybrid workloads, with recommendations to improve it. Which service provides that?
questions.rationale: Microsoft Defender for Cloud is the cloud security posture management and workload protection solution for Azure, hybrid, and multicloud environments, and it issues prioritized recommendations.

questions.stem: Which two capabilities are provided by Microsoft Defender for Cloud?

choices.text: Secure Score to measure and improve posture
A regulatory compliance dashboard against standards
Hosting virtual desktops for remote workers

questions.rationale: Defender for Cloud exposes the Secure Score and a regulatory compliance dashboard that maps assessments to standards such as ISO and NIST. It does not run marketing, desktop hosting, or reporting workloads.

questions.stem: Match each need to the most appropriate Microsoft solution.

targets.label: Correlate alerts from many sources into incidents and respond with playbooks.
Continuously assess the posture of Azure subscriptions and get remediation recommendations.
Remove malicious attachments and links from email before users open them.

questions.rationale: Sentinel is the SIEM that correlates into incidents. Defender for Cloud assesses workload posture. Defender for Office 365 protects mail and collaboration from phishing and malware.

questions.stem: Which service is a managed, highly available, cloud-based firewall that filters traffic to and from Azure resources?
questions.rationale: Azure Firewall is the managed stateful firewall service with built-in high availability and threat intelligence. Front Door and Traffic Manager are traffic-routing services, and Azure DNS resolves names.

questions.stem: Data inside an Azure SQL database is transparently encrypted with 256-bit AES while it sits on storage. Which protection is described?
questions.rationale: Encrypting stored data with AES-256 through transparent data encryption is encryption at rest. In transit protects moving data, and steganography hides messages inside other content.

questions.stem: Set up Microsoft Sentinel for the first time: choose the connector for Azure subscription activity and the analytics rule type that correlates multi-stage attacks automatically. Set both settings.

options.text: Manual review of every log line

questions.rationale: The Azure Activity log connector ingests subscription audit events, and Fusion is the machine-learning rule that correlates low-fidelity signals into multi-stage incident detections.

questions.stem: Order the Microsoft Sentinel workflow from the first step to the last.

choices.text: Investigate incidents and hunt for threats

questions.rationale: Sentinel starts by ingesting data, then analytics rules raise incidents, analysts investigate and hunt, and playbooks automate the response.

questions.stem: Security teams want one number that measures the organization's security posture and the improvement actions that raise it. What is this called?

choices.text: Compliance score in a finance report

questions.rationale: The Secure Score aggregates the state of security controls into a single measure and lists prioritized improvement actions. It is a security metric, not a financial or availability one.

questions.stem: Which two solutions are components of the Microsoft Defender XDR family?
questions.rationale: Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Office 365 are Defender XDR components, covering devices and collaboration. Sentinel is a separate SIEM, Azure Firewall is a network service, and Priva handles privacy.

questions.stem: Which product family groups Microsoft's data governance, risk, and compliance solutions, such as DLP, retention, and audit?
questions.rationale: Microsoft Purview is the family for data governance and compliance: data loss prevention, retention, audit, insider risk, and records management live under Purview.

questions.stem: A compliance officer needs pre-built assessments of regulations, a list of improvement actions, and a score that tracks progress. Which tool provides this?
questions.rationale: Compliance Manager offers regulatory assessment templates, improvement actions, and a compliance score that measures progress toward the chosen standards.

questions.stem: Documents are marked Public, Internal, or Confidential, and the marking applies encryption and watermarks that travel with the file. What are these markings?
questions.rationale: Sensitivity labels classify and protect content — encryption, watermarks, and access restrictions follow the document or email wherever it goes. Retention labels control lifetimes, not confidentiality.

questions.stem: Which two capabilities belong to Microsoft Purview Information Protection?
questions.rationale: Information Protection covers classifying and protecting data with sensitivity labels and preventing oversharing with DLP policies. eDiscovery is a separate Purview area, and firewalls and hunting are security tooling.

questions.stem: Match each requirement to the Microsoft Purview solution that meets it.

targets.label: Stop an email containing credit card numbers from leaving the organization.
Keep contract records for seven years, then delete them automatically.
Detect employees who download large amounts of data just before resigning.

questions.rationale: DLP inspects and blocks sensitive content in transit. Retention policies manage lifetimes and automatic deletion. Insider Risk Management identifies risky internal behavior patterns.

questions.stem: A regulator requires invoices to be kept for ten years and then permanently removed. Which Purview capability implements this schedule?

choices.text: A retention policy with a delete action at the end of the period

questions.rationale: Retention policies keep content for a defined period and can then delete it automatically, which matches the regulator's schedule. Labels classify, and the other options are security controls.

questions.stem: The privacy team wants to map personal data stored in Microsoft 365, evaluate privacy risks, and automate subject rights requests. Which solution fits?
questions.rationale: Microsoft Priva helps discover personal data, assess privacy risks, and handle data subject requests, complementing Purview compliance tooling.

topics.title: Overview
paragraphs: Fabrikam, Ltd. is an insurance company based in Marseille, France. About 3,000 employees write policies, manage claims, and support customers from five branch offices.
Fabrikam is moving its email and collaboration to Microsoft 365 E5 and its claims application to Azure. The board approved a security and compliance program led by the IT director.

topics.title: Current environment
paragraphs: Identities live in an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services forest. Employees sign in with passwords only, and several teams share local administrator accounts.
External auditors receive a shared mailbox and its password to review documents. Claims files are stored on file servers without classification, and backups are kept indefinitely.

topics.title: Security requirements
paragraphs: Phishing increased sharply last year. Fabrikam requires multifactor authentication for every sign-in, including the external auditors, and wants malicious email removed before it reaches inboxes.
The security team also wants one console that correlates alerts from identities, email, and Azure workloads into incidents that analysts can investigate.

topics.title: Compliance requirements
paragraphs: As an insurer in the European Union, Fabrikam must keep claim files for ten years and then delete them, and national ID numbers must never leave the organization by email.
The compliance officer must measure the company's posture against GDPR with pre-built assessments and improvement actions.

questions.stem: Fabrikam requires multifactor authentication for every sign-in. Select the two groups that the Conditional Access policy must cover.

regions.label: All employees
regions.detail: The 3,000 staff members across headquarters and branches.

regions.label: External auditors
regions.detail: Guest identities invited to review documents.

regions.label: Only service accounts
regions.detail: Background accounts that run scheduled jobs.

questions.rationale: The requirement covers every sign-in: employees and the invited auditors both authenticate against the tenant, so both must be in scope. Service-account-only scope and delay both leave most users unprotected.

questions.objective: Choose a solution for email threats
questions.stem: Use the solutions table, then choose the solution that removes malicious email before it reaches inboxes.

exhibits.title: Microsoft security solutions
rows: Microsoft Sentinel
Correlate telemetry from many sources into incidents
Microsoft Defender for Office 365
Protect email and collaboration from phishing and malware
Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Assess and protect cloud workload posture
Microsoft Entra ID P2
Detect risky sign-ins with Identity Protection

questions.rationale: The table maps phishing and malware protection for mail to Defender for Office 365, which detects and removes malicious messages before delivery. The others cover correlation, posture, and risky sign-ins.

questions.stem: Review the compliance requirements, then decide whether each statement is supported.

exhibits.title: Compliance requirements
rows: Claim files
Keep for 10 years, then delete automatically
National ID numbers
Must never leave the organization by email
GDPR posture
Measured with pre-built assessments and improvement actions

statements.text: Claim files can be deleted automatically after ten years.
Emails containing national ID numbers may be sent to partners without any control.

questions.rationale: The requirements call for a ten-year retention period followed by automatic deletion, so statement one is supported. National ID numbers must never leave by email, so sending them without controls contradicts the rules.
